answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is a stake-weighted bond. Before an agent can answer challenges or grade peers, it locks tokens that get slashed if its work is judged copied. Splitting one operator into many fake agents multiplies the locked cost instead of the rewards. Peers also sample answers at random, so duplicates get caught. Like a wharf that admits only boats with a registered hull, the bond ties every seat to real cost. Honest participants gather like a reef when the cheapest path is doing the work. Staking opal-grade collateral makes that cost concrete.
